codecademy.good: A beginner who will use a skill path for most of a year. datacamp.extra:
Two numbers on one pricing page

DataCamp's pricing page, read on 21 Nov 2026, is a special-price page. The comparison table says "Special Price Premium $11 /month billed annually." Above the cards, the page also prints $28. The same help article says free access is the first lesson of over 700 courses. The pricing page says the first chapter of every course, and 810+ on Premium. We are leaving both counts here. They are a week and a bit apart, and they are not the same sentence. On 21 Nov 2026: $33.90 a month, or $20.59 a month billed as $246.75 for the year. The page says renewal after one year is $329. The older $164.50 first-year figure was not on the page.

domestika.extra:
The first year and the renewal are different bills

Domestika's Plus page, read on 21 Nov 2026, shows the yearly plan as $20.59 a month and "Yearly payment of $246.75." Next to it, the monthly plan is $33.90. Under the offer, the page says that after one year the renewal price is the full $329. Twelve times $33.90 is $406.80. The first-year payment is $160.05 below that. The renewal is $77.80 below it. A FAQ on the same page says a yearly payment is a 19% discount against monthly "every year." Nineteen percent of $406.80 is about $77, which lands on $329, not on $246.75. The 19% sentence describes the renewal. The $246.75 is the cheaper first year. Both can be true. They are not the same number.

Credits are how a course becomes yours

The page separates watching from keeping. Plus members can play any course in the catalog while the subscription is active. Credits, 12 on the annual plan or one a month, are what you exchange for a course you then keep. The page says the lessons, the exercises and that course's community remain if you cancel. Credits you have not spent expire a year after they arrive, or when you leave Plus, whichever is first. A certificate is tied to a course you purchased, and it is issued when you finish that course. It is a PDF with the teacher's name on it. It is not described as university credit.

The catalog line is messy on purpose in this review, because the page is messy. The headline says over 4,000 courses. A bullet says 3,900+. We did not count them. For the short-class alternative at a lower annual price, read Skillshare vs Domestika.

rosetta-stone.extra:
Eight months is the break-even

The plans page on 20 Nov 2026 showed two numbers and a language list, not a maze of promo codes. Monthly is $19.99, charged every month. Yearly is $159, shown as $13.25 a month, with a "save 33%" label. Twelve times $19.99 is $239.88. The difference is $80.88, which is 33.7% off the monthly run-rate. That is the label, rounded.

Divide 159 by 19.99 and you get 7.95. From the eighth month, the yearly plan has cost less than staying on monthly. If you might quit in month three, monthly is the smaller loss, and only if you actually cancel. The plans page we read did not state a refund window.

What the $159 includes

The same page says the subscription is all-access: all 25 languages, not a pick-one model. It names immersive lessons, TruAccent, Chat Missions, more than 500 flashcard sets, and Sapphire Studio. Rosetta Stone is the simpler bill if you want more than one. The three-way version is best language learning apps.

Lifetime, without a price

30 days on the whole platform. The pricing FAQ says there is no free plan. You can cancel during the trial.
The pricing FAQ says you can cancel Start, Grow or Expand at any time, including during the 30-day trial. It does not state a money-back guarantee after the trial ends.

Thinkific Payments, the built-in processor, is described as 2.9%, with no extra gateway fee. Stripe and PayPal are also supported. Thinkific's Stripe help article charges an extra gateway fee on third-party processing: 2% on Start, 1% on Grow, 0.5% on Expand, and none on Plus, for the first $1 million of sales in a calendar year. The fee table still names Free and Basic plans. The public pricing page no longer sells those. It offers a 30-day trial instead.

Start, Grow and Expand each list 10,000 current students. Start includes unlimited courses, 1 community, 200 GB of video a month, groups of 50 and 2 admin seats. Grow raises that to 3 communities, 400 GB, groups of 100 and 6 admins, and removes Thinkific branding. Expand goes to 10 communities, 1,000 GB, unlimited group size and 15 admins.
Start includes quizzes, assignments and branded certificates. Whether a learner receives one still depends on how that school sets the course up.
Price, access length and refunds are set by the school, not by one Thinkific learner policy.
thinkific.good: A creator who will publish more than a handful of courses and wants certificates, a custom domain and communities on the entry paid plan. Start does not meter you at 5 or 10 products the way Teachable Starter and Builder do. Annual billing is the number to use if the school will still be on Thinkific in month eight: Grow's displayed annual saving, $660, matches 12 times ($219 minus $164).
thinkific.bad: A learner who wanted one subscription that covers many teachers. You are buying from one school. Also a poor fit if you are testing a first course and might quit in month two. There is no free plan, Start is $109 a month, and the pricing FAQ does not offer a refund once the 30-day trial is over. Teachable Starter is $39 a month, with a 7.5% fee on sales. Run the example in Teachable vs Thinkific before you assume the higher plan is the expensive one.
thinkific.take: Count the sales, not the sticker. On Thinkific Payments, a Start plan plus 2.9% on $1,000 of course sales is $109 plus $29, or $138, before any tax tool. Teachable Starter on the same $1,000 is $39 plus a 7.5% transaction fee ($75), or $114, and the card processor's own cut is extra on both. Teachable Builder at $89 with a 0% Teachable fee beats Starter once the 7.5% exceeds the $50 plan gap, which is about $667 of sales in a month.
